correctness.rationale: The geometric fixed set is the orbit-centroid subcomplex: its vertices are invariant orbit simplices and joins require all cross-orbit vertex distances <= r. For a weight-one generator the cross-max is 1+d(y,z); for either two-dimensional allowable subgroup it is 2+d(y,z). For a two-bit flip, same-color cross-max is 2+d and different-color is 1+d. The r=2 orbit graph has 2^(n-1) vertices and is a standard cube graph; its integral cycle rank is 1+2^(n-2)(n-3). At r=3 all newly added edges reduce through triangles to the cube graph, whose elementary squares bound cones, so pi_1 vanishes. The argument extends to all later scales by shortening new edges. Exact shift models give the stated low-degree barcodes, with no torsion. Signed edge/vertex permutation traces in 0 -> L -> C1 -> C0 -> Z ->0 yield tr(0,h)=1-f+2e and tr(1,h)=1-q. Independently enumerated every coset and cross-distance for 89 (n,type,scale) cases n=2..7; all agreed. These bounded cases support, but do not replace, the stated all-n proof.
